data.message: Retrieving the official financial statement PDF from the CSE document repository
Document secured and staged for processing
Running multi-dimensional financial health diagnostics with LLM (this may take a minute)...
Health diagnostics finalised for CARG.N0000 — overall score: 80/100 · Good

standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: The Group operates with a current ratio of 0.75 and a quick ratio of 0.34 due to negative working capital (-Rs. 17.73 billion). While typical for retail operators with fast cash collection cycles, high short-term interest-bearing liabilities (Rs. 22.74 billion) keep short-term liquidity tight.

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Profit After Tax (PAT) expanded 49.8% YoY to Rs. 10.89 billion. The Group achieved a solid Return on Equity (ROE) of 23.90% and Return on Assets (ROA) of 7.50%, supported by revenue growth of 12.74% YoY despite macro headwinds and cost pressures.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Interest coverage remains comfortable at 4.42x. Total net debt reduced from Rs. 20.3 billion to Rs. 16.1 billion over the past 12 months. Borrowings-to-Equity ratio stands at 0.50x (1.06x including lease liabilities).

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Operating cash flow was outstanding at Rs. 18.03 billion, comfortably exceeding net profit (165% earnings conversion). Free cash flow generation reached approximately Rs. 12.05 billion after accounting for capital expenditure.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Same-Store Sales Growth (SSSG) & Store Expansion
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Retail same-store sales grew 12.3% and Restaurant SSSG reached 14.0%. The Retail segment added 17 new outlets during the year (bringing store count to 560), while Restaurants expanded with 12 new KFC outlets.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: SSSG and physical footprint growth are key revenue drivers for superstores and restaurant chains, indicating core customer retention and brand health.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Operating Overhead & Supply Chain Cost Efficiency
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Distribution costs jumped 34.65% YoY, driven by higher electricity tariffs and staff expenses. In addition, raw milk supply fell ~20% following Cyclone Ditwah livestock losses, putting margin pressure on FMCG dairy operations.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) and Retail operate on tight margins where energy, distribution, and commodity supply shocks directly impact operating profitability.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Segment Diversification & Operational Resilience
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Strong performance across Retail (+10.5% segment revenue) and FMCG (+20.9% segment revenue) offset property write-downs, Cyclone Ditwah disruptions (Rs. 858M gross loss), and the discontinuation of the TGI Fridays franchise.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: A diversified multi-segment strategy (Retail, FMCG, Restaurants, Real Estate) buffers conglomerates against localized sector downturns and natural disaster losses.

recommendations: Refinance or optimize short-term borrowings (Rs. 22.74 billion) into longer-tenor structures to improve the current ratio and ease short-term liquidity pressure.
Implement energy-efficiency initiatives and route optimization across retail outlets and distribution networks to curb rising electricity and transport overheads.
Strengthen direct dairy farmer engagement and sourcing logistics to mitigate the 20% national milk supply deficit caused by Cyclone Ditwah.
Restructure capital allocation for Real Estate developments at Katubedda and Bandarawela to ensure property rental cash flows adequately cover associated interest expenses.
result.analysisNotes: Cargills (Ceylon) PLC demonstrated impressive financial resilience during FY 2025/26, with revenue reaching Rs. 272.7 billion and operating profit growing 22.9% YoY. Excellent operating cash generation allowed the Group to pay down net debt while continuing store network expansion. Primary risks remain macro-driven inflation, energy tariff increases, and tight short-term liquidity ratios.
